_doc: PRIOR ART: scripts/eval/DECISIONS.md (the per-stratum ledger: what was measured and who decided, one row per question, 80+ rows), .claude/docs/ocr-engine-routing.md (a generated per-LANGUAGE table of what the Gemini router does), .claude/docs/ocr-lane-decision-tree.md (the operator's tree for a page that needs text). None answers in one lookup 'this KIND of page: which reader, and why', and none is read by the public /quality page. This file is that lookup (#6688) and the only copy: scripts/lib/ocr-routing.mjs exports it (OCR_ROUTING_TABLE, ocrRouteForKind), the table in scripts/eval/ocr-routing/README.md is generated from it (node scripts/eval/build-routing-table.mjs), /quality renders `kind`, `reader`, `why` and the first evidence link, and tests/unit/ocr-routing-table.test.ts checks all three plus every `code` claim against the live router and lane files. It RECORDS routing; it does not change what any lane selects. To change a row: change it here in the same PR as the experiment file that justifies it, then re-run the builder.

fields.kind: public: the kind of page, in plain words
fields.why: public: one or two sentences, measured figures with n and date (quality-statements.md)
fields.in_use: public: whether production does this today, in one plain sentence (agrees with `routed`)
fields.status: settled = measured and decided; provisional = decided on thin or by-eye evidence; open = no reader chosen on evidence yet
fields.routed: yes = production does this today; partly = some pages; no = evidence says so, production does not do it yet
fields.production: internal: what production does today and where
fields.code: internal, checked by the test: {router: a probe of getOcrModelForBook and the model it must return} or {file: a lane or reader script that must exist}
fields.evidence: the experiment files (scripts/eval/experiments/) or issue behind the row, with the sample and the date
fields.audit: the weekly audit stratum (scripts/eval/ocr-routing/README.md, "The weekly audit"): how the lane's pages are selected, and which model family reviews them (never the reader's own)
fields.pareto: optional: the /quality/pareto chart this row's reader is the engine in use for, and that engine's id in the benchmark data. scripts/eval/build-ocr-pareto.mjs reads it; a chart no row names takes its engine in use from getOcrModelForBook
fields.stored: public: what readers have now, the stored text by the engine that wrote it, in pages, with the count it came from (the `census` block gives date, method and source; a row counted on another date says so); null where it was not counted. It differs from `reader`, which is what NEW pages get
fields.charts: optional: the /quality/pareto charts whose pages are this kind; build-ocr-pareto.mjs copies `stored` onto them so each chart names both baselines
fields.route: internal, READ BY THE ROUTER (#7170): what the code does for this kind. {engine, families: {<language family>: {from: date, hidden?: true}}}: getOcrModelForBook sends a book whose first language is in one of these families to `engine` (visible books, books created on or after `from`, and the hidden backlog too when `hidden`). {engine, default: true}: the model for every other book. {fallback: [{chart, engine, lane}], otherwise, source}: the next reader for a page Gemini refused, per estimator chart, never a Gemini model; `otherwise` for a page no chart covers; `source` is the derive_routes.py proposal it was adopted from. A row with no `route` routes nothing; with no family route anywhere the router keeps its pinned constants (FLASH_OCR_FROM_FALLBACK). A change to a route is proposed by scripts/eval/estimator/routing/derive_routes.py and lands as a reviewed diff of this field, never a silent edit.

rows.kind: Printed books in Latin, English, German, French and other languages in the Latin alphabet
rows.why: On 147 printed Latin pages with a typed reference (7 October 2026), Flash-Lite got 93.3% of characters right, Gemini 3 Flash 94.7% and Claude Sonnet 94.0%. No other engine we tested did better than Gemini 3 Flash, and the larger model costs about twice as much a page. On English print from 1800 to 1930 the two tied on 75 of 92 pages (114 books, September 2026). Known weakness: Flash-Lite reads the long s as f, and loops on some gothic type.
rows.stored: Mixed. Latin, 7,874,792 pages: 1,315,741 (17%) read by Gemini 3 Flash, 859,556 (11%) by Flash-Lite, 5,693,910 (72%) with no text yet. In the same order, German, 2,114,118 pages: 353,152 (17%), 418,010 (20%), 1,334,450 (63%). English, 1,705,755 pages: 503,256 (30%), 414,079 (24%), 502,398 (29%), and 271,203 (16%) with the Internet Archive's own text. French, 782,150 pages: 189,468 (24%), 151,451 (19%), 437,119 (56%). Italian, 310,814 pages: 118,056 (38%), 46,950 (15%), 143,959 (46%). Most of the pages with no text are in books first shown on 23 and 24 October 2026, most of them as page images only, for readers who read the original (#7176, #7270): 4,923,283 of the Latin ones, 1,207,466 German, 379,829 English, 406,892 French and 117,241 Italian. Of the Latin pages that have text, 60% were read by Gemini 3 Flash and 39% by Flash-Lite.
rows.production: getOcrModelForBook returns lite for every Latin-script language (and, under OCR_LITE_ONLY, for everything not in FLASH_OCR_FROM). Batch API.

The samples are small: the Pali and Arabic gains are not clearly above zero. Manuscripts in these languages are not covered.

rows.why: On 76 manuscript pages with an expert transcription (English, medieval Latin, French and Arabic; 12 October 2026), Opus got 9.9% of characters wrong, Gemini 3.1 Pro 14.0% and Flash-Lite 16.1%. Among each reader's ten worst pages, Opus wrote text that is not on the page on 3 and the Gemini readers on 5 to 7. Where Opus cannot read a line it marks it instead of guessing. On 40 of our own manuscript pages, which have no expert transcription, the order of Opus and Gemini 3.1 Pro depended on which model refereed, so that part is not settled.

Gemini 3.1 Pro was withdrawn from the agy CLI on 2026-10-12, so it is not an option.

rows.kind: Nahuatl and Mayan-language books (print and manuscript)
rows.why: In a first test on 18 pages, one per book (12 October 2026), Gemini 3.8 Flash rewrote colonial Mayan letters as modern ones 24 times on 8 pages. In a check of 15 Opus-read pages from 3 books (13 October 2026), a Gemini reviewer scored them 3.80 of 5, just under the 4.0 we had set, found no invented text, and caught 3 of 3 errors we had planted. The pages had no text before, so they were filled with this reading.

rows.kind: Chinese: the Siku Quanshu, a library copied by hand in regular script
rows.why: On 433 books, one page each (1 October 2026), PaddleOCR got more than half the characters wrong on 0.9% of pages, Gemini 3 Flash on 3.7% and Flash-Lite on 10.6%. In a random check of 60 pages PaddleOCR had read, one per book (10 October 2026), no page was unusable and none had invented text: 51% were clean, 27% had minor errors and 22% had material errors. Qwen3-VL tied it on 503 pages at three times the cost.
rows.stored: Counted across all Chinese books, 1,943,433 Chinese pages: 1,599,766 (82%) read by PaddleOCR-VL, 103,874 (5%) by Gemini 3 Flash, 18,720 (1%) by Flash-Lite, 4,521 by Claude Opus, and 214,554 (11%) with no text yet.
rows.production: scripts/lib/paddle-zh-lane.mjs (ocr.source 'paddle'), run by hand on a leased GPU over fixed book lists (#5600, #5660, #6388); 1.57M pages written. Not in lanes.mjs, and no scheduled lane selects its books: they are held. Measured 2026-10-13 from books.pages_count − pages_ocr: about 68K unread Chinese pages sit in books held for this lane (holds gpu-backlog-5660, paddle-zh-5600-ocr-only, paddle-zh-6388-*) and wait for its next run.

rows.kind: Chinese pages with tables and diagrams
rows.reader: PaddleOCR-VL, then Claude Opus corrects the draft against the image
rows.why: PaddleOCR invents text on table pages. A rule on the text found all 136 pages known to have invented text and flags 4,379 of 1,568,108 pages (0.28%), which are withheld (11 October 2026). On 40 of them (12 October 2026), Opus correcting the draft left 4.0% of characters wrong, against 6.4% for the draft and 5.8% for Opus reading the image afresh. It was better on 31 pages and worse on 1. Opus reading from the image alone was not adopted: a Gemini reviewer found invented text in 23 of 100 such readings.
rows.in_use: In use on the 4,379 flagged pages: they show the corrected text.

The check caught all 8 pages where PaddleOCR repeated or dropped text, and passed 34 of 35 good pages. Two works are not read this way, because neither reader gets them right: a five-script glossary and a book of qin tablature.

rows.kind: Chinese woodblock and typeset print outside the Siku Quanshu
rows.reader: PaddleOCR-VL, one leaf at a time; Gemini 3 Flash for the pages its checks turn away
rows.why: Measured on 22 October 2026 against a typed text of the same editions, on 198 pages from 54 books, with each spread split into its two leaves: PaddleOCR-VL got a median 6.1% of characters wrong, Gemini 3 Flash 5.2% and Flash-Lite 6.7%. PaddleOCR-VL had 3 pages more than half wrong, all of them blank leaves, which the checks now turn away; Flash-Lite also had 3, and Flash none. Flash is still the more accurate reader. PaddleOCR-VL runs on our own GPU at no cost per page, which keeps the Gemini allowance for correcting text (Derek, 26 October 2026).
rows.in_use: In use for the Chinese print books read in October 2026. Pages its checks turn away wait for Gemini 3 Flash, and books outside that read go to Gemini 3 Flash.
rows.stored: Counted with all Chinese books, 1,943,433 pages: 103,874 (5%) read by Gemini 3 Flash, 18,720 (1%) by Flash-Lite, 1,599,766 (82%) by PaddleOCR-VL, and 214,554 (11%) with no text yet.
rows.production: scripts/workers/paddle-print-lane.mjs (ocr.pipeline paddle-print-2026-10, ocr.source paddle), run by hand on gex45 through /root/gpu-queue over a frame of print books outside the Siku, cursive-Japanese and Meiji-typeset cohorts (#6101, PR #7211). Each spread is split at the gutter; per leaf the lane turns away faint leaves (show-through), unstable short leaves (re-read at 1,200 px disagrees), under-read leaves, loops, textless spreads, kana-heavy (Japanese) books and pages that lost their ditto marks; it never replaces a Gemini Flash / Pro, Claude, CBETA or human text, and replaces flash-lite only when it covers lite's text. Books are held paddle-print-6101 before the first write. Written 2026-10-25: 73,330 pages. Census 2026-10-26 (job paddle-print-rest-6101): no unread non-Siku Chinese print book is left outside that frame; the next frame is the Berlin State Library import (#7343, held manifest-only-lazy-pages, no page records yet). The fallback is wired (job paddle-rejects-flash-6101, 2026-10-26): the lane's apply lists every page its checks turned away that is still without text (fallbackRoute: guard rejects to Flash, textless pages with every leaf blank or faint left unread, pages with no image to the fetch lane), and `paddle-print-lane.mjs fallback --read --apply` reads that list with Gemini 3.8 Flash through agy (scripts/batch/cli-ocr.mjs, its guards and provenance); the book keeps its hold. Everything outside the lane: FLASH_OCR_FROM.zho (#7075, from 2026-10-21): getOcrModelForBook returns flash for visible Chinese books and Chinese books created from that date, and flash runs only through the agy CLI: the orchestrator holds the book (CLI_FLASH_OCR_HOLD, reason ocr-flash-cli-7075) for scripts/batch/cli-ocr.mjs instead of submitting it to the Batch API. Hidden Chinese books created before the date stay on lite, Batch. Books held for the Siku Paddle lane (row chinese-siku-manuscript) keep that hold.

rows.reader: BDRC Yigdzin, a reader built for Tibetan
rows.why: On 60 Kangyur pages (6 October 2026), Yigdzin matched 94.9% of the syllables of the typed Derge text. Claude Opus, the best general model, matched 71.5% and fell below half on 4 of the 60 pages. On one page checked by eye it wrote Tibetan that is not on the leaf. On 30 folios (12 and 13 October 2026), a model correcting the Yigdzin text against the image raised the match: Gemini 3.8 Flash to 96.8% with no folio worse and 3 of 30 planted errors left, Opus to 96.0% with 14 of 30 left. Reading afresh from the image lowered it to 70%. On 60 Kangyur folios judged against the image (26 and 27 October 2026), the Yigdzin text was accepted as the page's transcription on 34, after a Gemini 3.8 Flash correction on 53, and after an Opus correction on 52. Applied to a whole volume (525 pages, 26 October 2026), the Flash correction made 6 of 40 checked pages worse, more than the 4 allowed, so it is not applied.
rows.in_use: In use. The Flash correction is not: it failed its check on the first volume.
rows.stored: 430,518 pages: 280,623 (65%) read by Yigdzin and 1,836 by BDRC's woodblock model. 137,535 (32%) carry Esukhia's digital text of the Derge Kangyur and Tengyur, matched to the page. 9,352 (2%) still carry a Gemini reading, and 1,172 have no text yet.
rows.production: Per-leaf Yigdzin read, verdicts applied by scripts/maintenance/apply-reocr-verdicts.mjs (ocr.source 'bdrc'). Lite is unusable as a Tibetan reader (#4523). Correction stage (#6560): Yigdzin > Gemini 3.8 Flash-low correction via agy, the #6560 CORR prompt (scripts/eval/tibetan-correct-6560/corr-prompt.txt), gated per volume (scripts/eval/tibetan-correct-6560/pass/run-pass.sh; ya-btags guard, 25% syllable cap, ocr.pipeline tib-correct-6560, no --mark-stale). The router picks it: router-table cell tibetan-yigdzin (scripts/eval/estimator/router-table/2026-10-27-tibetan-30.md), accepted 53/60 vs Yigdzin 34/60 and Opus correction 52/60, switch -> yigdzin>agy-flash-low. Its first volume gate failed (2026-10-26, Thadrak Kanjur rGyud 'bum Ka 69e7aab880b52390feb197a8: pooled worse 6/40, bar <= 4 and better >= 3x worse; tiled span judge 6/40 worse, whole-page judge 5/40), so nothing is applied and the pass is stopped until a new pre-registered corrector passes the same gate.

evidence.n: one volume, 525 pages; 40 changed pages judged by two Opus judges

audit.reviewer: claude and gemini (the reader is neither family)

rows.reader: Kraken, an open-source reader, with a model trained on Syriac
rows.why: On 20 printed books, one page each (8 October 2026), Kraken got 13.0% of consonants wrong, Gemini 3.7 Flash 42.6% and Flash-Lite 68.3%. On 350 pages of the 1905 Syriac New Testament (16 September 2026), Gemini 3 Flash gave the right passage with at most 10% of letters wrong on 19% of pages, a different passage on 14%, and text that is not in the Bible on 17%. English made from the Kraken text scored 1.33 of 5 points lower than English made from a typed text, so those translations are withheld.
rows.production: scripts/lib/syriac-kraken-lane.mjs on Hetzner CPU (ocr.source 'kraken'). Never Gemini (Derek, #4883).

audit.reviewer: claude and gemini (the reader is neither family)

rows.why: Checked by eye, not against a typed text. On 20 cursive books (30 September 2026) it gave the text of the page on 9 of 10 pages we read, where Gemini's earlier reading was invented or looping on 3 of 4. There is no accuracy figure yet because we have no typed reference for these pages.

rows.production: scripts/lib/ndl-koten-lane.mjs (ocr.source 'ndl-koten'), pilot of 20 books (PR #5412); no standing lane (#5100). Typeset Japanese is unmeasured and reads on lite.

audit.reviewer: claude and gemini (the reader is neither family)

rows.kind: A page Gemini declines to read because it recognises a famous published text
rows.reader: A second try, then MinerU (an open-source reader) for English printed after 1820, then the Internet Archive's own text if a person has checked it
rows.why: On 114 English books, one page each (30 September 2026), MinerU read all 16 pages Gemini had refused. On all pages its typical error was 0.66% of characters against 0.20% for Flash-Lite, so it fills gaps and does not replace Flash-Lite. The Internet Archive's own text gets 5.1% of printed numbers wrong against 1.8% for Flash-Lite (82 books, 5,212 numbers), so it is used only for pages with no other text.
rows.production: The RECITATION ladder (ocr-lane-decision-tree.md, branch 3): lite again, flash (= lite under OCR_LITE_ONLY, ocrEscalationModel), scripts/workers/mineru-ocr-worker.mjs (1820+ only: before that it reads the long s as f), ia-ocr-ingest under a by-eye verdict, then by eye.

audit.reviewer: claude and gemini (the reader is neither family)

rows.kind: A page where two readings disagree
rows.reader: Claude Opus compares both with the image and decides; Gemini checks a sample of the changes
rows.why: On 150 of the most-read books that are not in English (1,491 pages, 13 October 2026), a second reading by Gemini was compared with the stored text, and Opus settled each difference against the image. 214 pages (14%) were rewritten and Opus kept the stored text on 543. In a blind check of 78 rewritten pages, Opus judged none worse than before and Gemini judged 4 worse; those 4 were not written. 34 pages in 12 books were withheld, among them a whole book showing the text of other pages.
rows.in_use: Used so far on the 200 most-read books that are not in English.
rows.production: scripts/batch/ocr-convergence/driver.mjs (#6420 lane B): Gemini CLI second read, Opus adjudicates every disagreement, a two-family audit gates the writes. Run on the 200 most-read non-English books; not a standing lane for the whole library.

audit.select: pages lane B wrote (page_revisions from ocr-convergence)
audit.reviewer: claude and gemini (already in the weekly audit)

rows.kind: A page that already has a text from a specialist reader, with some errors
rows.reader: A model corrects the existing text against the image; the page is not read again from nothing. Claude Opus for the Chinese table pages
rows.why: Measured on 12 and 13 October 2026. Tibetan, 30 folios: correcting raised the match with the typed Derge text from 94.5% to 96.0% (Opus) and 96.8% (Gemini 3.8 Flash), and reading afresh lowered it to 70%. Chinese, 40 table pages: Opus correcting left 4.0% of characters wrong, reading afresh 5.8%. Smaller Claude models did not correct as well: Sonnet made 10 of 40 pages worse where Opus made 1.
rows.in_use: In progress on the Chinese table pages. Not yet used for Tibetan.
rows.production: Applied to the Chinese table pages only (job table-correct-6561, files, not yet written). Tibetan: the router picks Yigdzin > Flash-low correction (#6740), but its first volume gate failed on 2026-10-26 (6/40 pages worse, bar 4), so none is applied (#6560, row tibetan). For manuscripts a correction pass was no better than Opus alone (#6544), so this row covers specialist drafts only.

not_adopted.engine: Other engines for print in the Latin alphabet and Greek (PaddleOCR-VL, olmOCR, GLM-OCR, Chandra, DeepSeek-OCR, Qwen3-VL, Mistral OCR)
not_adopted.why: None read Latin or Greek print better than Gemini 3 Flash. olmOCR read English of 1600 to 1699 better than Flash-Lite, but it was not adopted and the lanes on our own GPU were stopped (#5660, #5924, #6011).

not_adopted.engine: Claude Sonnet and Haiku as correctors
not_adopted.why: Neither corrects a draft as well as Opus (#6667).
No longer offered by the subscription tool we use (since 12 October 2026). Where measured, it did not beat Opus on manuscripts (#6544) and made 21 of 40 Chinese table pages worse (#6561).

not_adopted.engine: Any general model as a Tibetan or Syriac reader
not_adopted.why: They write text that is not on the page, or write out a known edition instead of reading the page (#4523, #4883, #6011).

census.source: scripts/eval/ocr-routing/stored-census.mjs (output: scripts/eval/ocr-routing/stored-census-2026-10-25.json), run 2026-10-25 over twelve languages, Chinese and Tibetan included: 16,178,325 pages in 64,624 live books
census.method: Every page of every live book (visible, pages_count > 0), grouped by books.language and counted by the engine whose text the page carries now (ocr.model); a page with no text counts as no text yet, and a page whose text names no engine is counted as unrecorded (all 137,535 such pages are Tibetan, and their ocr.source is Esukhia's Derge Kangyur or Tengyur text). It replaces the counts of 2026-10-16 and, for Chinese and Tibetan, of 2026-10-13. Books first shown on 23 and 24 October 2026 (#7176, #7270) are counted with the rest. An earlier draw of 150 random books per language was dropped: a few long books carry most of the pages, so two draws of 300 Latin books gave 22% and 29% with no text.

page_check._doc: Display only: /quality renders it under the page-kind table, and the `in_use` sentences of routes not in use also under the matching row's reader (`row`). It routes nothing. Every accepted / wrong_text count is the route's cell in `source` (score.json), checked by tests/unit/ocr-routing-table.test.ts. The judge accepts a page when a reader would be served by publishing it as that page's text (for a translation: its statements, negations, names and numbers), and marks wrong text when the candidate says something the page does not: invented, duplicated, dropped, another page, or a wrong word that changes the sense (scripts/eval/route-judge-6740/judge.mjs).

routes.wrong_text_what: Mostly words or whole lines left out (9 pages) and misreads that make another word (7). Some reverse the sense: “inæquales” read as “equales”, “ſeminis” (of seed) as “feminis” (of women).

routes.reader: Flash-Lite, then Claude Opus corrects the text against the image
routes.wrong_text_what: None. What is left is cosmetic, for example abbreviations expanded on some lines and not on others.

kinds.kind: Chinese pages that PaddleOCR-VL read and a rule flagged as possibly invented (4,379 pages, mostly the Siku Quanshu)

routes.reader: PaddleOCR-VL, then Claude Opus corrects the draft against the image
routes.in_use: In use on the flagged pages.
routes.wrong_text_what: On 3 pages that are mostly Manchu, the Manchu is left out (a note in the text says so). On the one table page the counting-rod numbers are written right to left, so each reads reversed.

routes.in_use: What these pages had before the correction.
routes.wrong_text_what: Lines left out (14 pages), misreads that make another character (12), repeated text (12) and text that is not on the page (8).

kinds.note: An upper bound. Of the 3 corrected pages we read by eye, one changes the calligrapher's name 章德懋 to 童德懋, twice, where the page and PaddleOCR's draft have 章; the reviewer accepted it. Other one-character changes to names may have passed the same way.

routes.wrong_text_what: Misreads that make another word (6 folios), one of which loses a negation; lines or phrases left out (4); syllables that are not on the leaf (2).

routes.reader: Yigdzin, then Gemini 3.8 Flash corrects the text against the image
routes.wrong_text_what: On one folio it filled a line Yigdzin had dropped with words that are not on the leaf. On another it put in “desire” from a different formula where the leaf has “ignorance”.

routes.reader: Yigdzin, then Claude Opus corrects the text against the image
routes.wrong_text_what: A phrase copied ahead from the next line, a garbled phrase, a doubled syllable.

kinds.kind: German books printed 1500 to 1800: the English translation
kinds.sample: 30 pages, one per book, for each translator

routes.wrong_text_what: Misreads carried into the English (an alchemical sign, a family's coat of arms), a note taken from the next page, headwords left out. On 2 of the 6 the fault is in the page itself: its photo shows another page, or the edge of the facing one.
Text from the next page (3 pages), words or a clause left out (3), misreads (2: a planet's sign, “Venetian soap” as “Benedetto powders”), a sense turned around (1).
A word dropped at a bracket, a claim about earlier pages, and a page whose photo shows another page (a fault in the page, not the translation).

kinds.note: Each translator was judged on its own 30 pages, so the comparison is between samples, not page by page.
